findings.stemStart: Quarter bottles and the giant formats beyond a
findings.problem: Old stem: 'Quarter bottles and jeroboams are often filled from wine that fermented in an ordinary bottle, ...'. In Champagne the jeroboam (3 L) is the largest format that must stay in the bottle it fermented in. Transfer is allowed only below the half bottle and above the jeroboam, so the stem taught the boundary the wrong way round.
findings.fix: Stem now reads 'Quarter bottles and the giant formats beyond a jeroboam are often filled from wine that fermented in an ordinary bottle, was emptied under pressure into a tank, filtered and bottled again. Which method is that?' Options, key and exp unchanged. Id moves i-5okaggzr to i-qqmopi1g; check-similarity clean (max ratio 0.556, run 4).
findings.source: Champagne appellation rule on bottle formats (transvasage only for formats smaller than a half bottle or larger than a jeroboam), as taught by GuildSomm's Champagne study guide and the standard sparkling syllabus.

findings.stemStart: Which German Pradikat level calls for individually selected,
findings.problem: The key, Trockenbeerenauslese (20 characters), stood 12 characters clear of Kabinett, Spatlese and Auslese (7 to 8). That is a visible length standout, so a student who knew no German law could pick the long word. Kabinett was also too weak a distractor for a botrytis question.
findings.fix: Kabinett is replaced with Beerenauslese. The key now stands 7 characters clear, below the standout line. The question now tests the real distinction: only Trockenbeerenauslese requires shrivelled berries, while Beerenauslese takes botrytised or overripe berries without it.
findings.source: German wine law (Weinverordnung): Beerenauslese from botrytised or at least overripe berries; Trockenbeerenauslese from largely shrivelled botrytised berries.

findings.stemStart: Which German Pradikat level calls for individually selected,
findings.problem: 'Beerenauslese sits just below it and Eiswein alongside' reads as Eiswein sharing the top level with Trockenbeerenauslese. Eiswein's legal minimum is Beerenauslese's must weight, not Trockenbeerenauslese's. The exp also never said why the key was right once Beerenauslese became a distractor.
findings.fix: Now: 'Trocken here means dried: the selected berries must have shrivelled almost to raisins under noble rot. Beerenauslese, one rung below, takes botrytised or overripe berries without demanding that shrivelling, and its minimum must weight is the one Eiswein has to reach. All three depend on the season, so they are made only in favourable years and in tiny quantities.'
findings.source: German wine law: Eiswein must reach at least the Beerenauslese must weight.

findings.stemStart: Between the two ways of warming Madeira, which
findings.problem: The stem frames a choice between two warming methods, but two of the four options ('Chilling the wine below freezing', 'Burying the casks in sand') were not ways of warming at all. That left a 50/50 between the only two options of the right kind.
findings.fix: Those two options are replaced with the swapped pairings 'Canteiro, tanks held near fifty degrees for months' and 'Estufa, years of gentle warmth in cask under the roof'. All four are now name plus method, and the student has to know both which name goes with which method and which method is kept for the finest wines. The key and exp are unchanged; the exp already names both methods correctly.
findings.source: Madeira rules: estufagem in heated tanks (about 45 to 50 C, at least three months) for everyday wine; canteiro, natural lodge warmth over years, for the finest.

findings.stemStart: Served cool alongside the cured pork and Parmigiano
findings.problem: 'The good bottles are dry and tank made' is false as a general rule: many of the most esteemed Lambruschi are refermented in bottle, by the ancestral or traditional method. 'A family of related varieties' also overstates it, since the Lambrusco varieties are distinct grapes sharing a name, not one close family.
findings.fix: Now: 'Lambrusco is a group of distinct local varieties sharing one name, grown around Modena and Reggio. The best are usually dry, whether tank made or refermented in bottle, and their acidity and light tannin cut straight through fat.'
findings.source: Lambrusco DOC rules allow both secondary fermentation in tank and in bottle; ampelographic work treats Sorbara, Grasparossa, Salamino and the rest as distinct varieties.

findings.stemStart: Fine, persistent bead and a bready character in
findings.problem: 'rests on its spent yeast inside that bottle for a year or more' is offered as true of the traditional method in general. It is not: Cava, the Cremants, Winzersekt and Cap Classique all have shorter legal minimums, nine months in the EU.
findings.source: EU minimum of nine months on the lees for traditional-method quality sparkling wine (Cava, Cremant, Winzersekt); Champagne's longer minimum is the exception.

findings.stemStart: Humid summers and Viognier make an unlikely pair,
findings.problem: The stem says 'one East Coast state', and Virginia was the only East Coast state among the options (Texas, Michigan, Idaho). The question answered itself from the options' geography.
findings.fix: The distractors are now North Carolina, Maryland and New Jersey, all East Coast wine-producing states, none built on Viognier. The key and exp are unchanged.
findings.source: Item construction rule: the stem must not be answerable from its own words or the options' shape. Viognier is Virginia's official state grape.

findings.fix: The key is trimmed to 'Much of the West is too dry to crop without it, and no AVA bars it' (65), now shorter than one distractor. The meaning is the same and the exp already carries the reasoning. Distractors unchanged.

findings.stemStart: In 1965 a grower planted Pinot Noir in
findings.problem: 'Within twenty years Burgundian houses were buying land nearby' is inexact: the first Burgundy house to buy in the Willamette Valley did so in 1987, twenty-two years on, and it was one house, not several, for a long time after.
findings.fix: Now 'By 1987 a Burgundy house had bought land nearby.'
findings.source: Maison Joseph Drouhin bought its Dundee Hills land in 1987; later Burgundian arrivals date from the 2010s.

findings.stemStart: Warm, flat and dependent on irrigation, the Central
findings.problem: 'Lodi sits at the northern end' (of the Central Valley) is wrong: the Central Valley runs on north through the Sacramento Valley to Redding. Lodi is at the northern end of the San Joaquin Valley, roughly the middle of the whole.
findings.fix: Now 'Lodi sits at the northern end of the San Joaquin Valley, cooled a little by air off the Sacramento Delta.'
findings.source: California geography: the Central Valley comprises the Sacramento Valley (north) and the San Joaquin Valley (south), meeting at the Delta beside Lodi.

findings.stemStart: A bottle says Cabernet Sauvignon on the front
findings.problem: 'Several states, Oregon among them, hold their producers to a stricter figure' asserts a plural I cannot support. Oregon is the established case of a stricter state varietal rule; I know of no other.
findings.fix: Now 'A state may demand more of its own producers, and Oregon does.' This is true whatever the count.
findings.source: Oregon's 90 percent varietal rule (OAR chapter 845, division 10) against the federal 75 percent (27 CFR 4.23).
